reason: Jung draws the conclusion in his own voice: 'It is clear from this that salt is an arcane substance', after surveying Turba/Senior/Arnaldus. Quote exact; jung-asserts is correct here because the identity statement is Jung's own inference, not a reported designation.

Mylius text quoted verbatim: 'our salt, that is, our earth... a dragon that eats his own tail'; ellipsis skips only 'and it is of a black colour' without distortion. Jung frames it as 'the identification of salt with the earth-dragon', so salt symbolized-by/identified-with uroboros via quoted Mylius is correct in direction and claim_type (jung-quotes-source, Mylius).
Jung asserts in his own voice: 'because of its proverbial whiteness salt is constantly associated with the albedo'. Quote exact, direction and claim_type correct.

The sentence is accurate ('without salt the opus will not succeed') but it carries footnote 429 and sits in a chain of reported alchemical maxims ('Our water cannot be made without salt' fn 428). Jung is summarizing alchemical doctrine, not asserting in his own psychological voice, so jung-asserts is the wrong claim_type.

Identity overreach as jung-asserts. The sentence 'salt is a spirit, a volatile substance, which the alchemists were wont to conceive as a bird' is footnoted (442) and explicitly framed as the alchemists' conception — Jung is explaining why the bird parallels salt in the sources, not asserting an identity himself.

'the Rosarium mentions that salt is bitter because it comes from the "mineral of the sea"' — derives-from direction correct (salt from sea), claim_type jung-reports-parallel with source Rosarium is exactly right for a reported designation.

§241: 'For Mylius it is synonymous with the tincture; it is the earth-dragon... and the "ash", the "diadem of thy heart"'. Salt = ash per Mylius; jung-reports-parallel with source Mylius correct; quote fragment accurate.

Jung's own interpretive summary: 'In other words, the ash is the spirit that dwells in the glorified body'. The 'in other words' marks it as Jung's own formulation, so jung-asserts fits; symbolizes is a fair rendering of the identity-as-interpretation.
Opening sentence in Jung's voice: 'Inseparable from salt and sea is the quality of amaritudo, bitterness'. Quote exact, direction fine.

'Among the best known synonyms for the latter [prima materia] are the "chaos" and the "sea"' — sea synonym-of prima materia, direction correct, Jung stating a fact about the tradition in his own voice.

The paragraph says the sea was 'conceived as the... matrix of all creatures' in the classical-mythological sense. Mapping 'matrix of all creatures' onto the Mother Archetype / Great Mother is an interpretive jump Jung does not make in this paragraph — no archetype language appears here.

Jerome quote verbatim and correctly attributed. The relation sea = devil's domain is carried by the whole paragraph (Augustine: 'element subject to the devil', 'realm of power allotted to the devil'); Jerome's sentence is a legitimate supporting quote. Direction correct (the sea is the devil's domain).

Augustine quote is verbatim, but he says the Red Sea signifies BAPTISM, and the paragraph speaks of 'healing and transforming baptismal water'. Rebirth/renovatio is not stated in §256 — object overreach (baptism connotes rebirth, but that link is not made here).

§256 says the Red Sea 'is thus an equivalent of the alchemical aqua pontica' — not aqua permanens. Jung equates pontica with permanens back in §244, but this edge's own paragraph names aqua pontica; object substituted across paragraphs.
'The "chariot of Aristotle" can be understood in this sense as a symbol of the self' — Jung's own conclusion after the quaternity analysis. Quote exact; jung-asserts correct.

'the quaternity embodied in it is the vehicle or throne of him who had the appearance of a man' — the Merkabah vehicle embodies the quaternity (= the four functions, the empirical self). Quote exact, direction acceptable, Jung's own psychological reading.

'The quaternity of the self appears in Ezekiel's vision as the true psychological foundation of the God-concept. God uses it as his vehicle.' Direction correct (quaternity is the foundation of the God-image/concept); jung-asserts correct — this is Jung's explicit empirical-psychological claim.

'the Garden of Eden was a favourite mandala... and is therefore a symbol of totality and—from the psychological point of view—of the self'. Quote exact; the psychological symbol-of-self claim is Jung's own.

'The Ortus is the alchemical "animal" which represents the living quaternity in its first synthesis' — Jung's own interpretive sentence; ellipsis in the quote omits only '"animal"' without distortion.
'Maier does not hesitate to identify the Ortus with the phoenix' — reported identification, correctly typed jung-reports-parallel with source Maier; direction correct.

The unification claim is explicitly attributed: 'As the "Tabula smaragdina" shows, the purpose of the ascent and descent is to unite the powers of Above and Below.' Per the reported-designation rule this cannot stand as bare jung-asserts; the authority is the Tabula Smaragdina (Jung endorses it, but the doctrine is sourced).

§296 says the ascent-descent dream motif 'corresponds to the struggle between the winged and the wingless dragon, i.e., the uroboros' — a correspondence/parallel between two expressions of the realization of opposites, not a symbol-referent relation. 'Symbolized-by' imposes an asymmetry the text does not state.
